mission: Build and validate a market-adaptive trade decision engine that produces a complete executable trade plan — setup, entry, invalidation/SL, TP1/TP2/TP3, sizing, management and exit — while maximizing net expectancy and opportunity capture under realistic costs, drawdown and overfitting controls.

separationFromPriorAlphaCampaign.reason: ITE1 is a new trade-construction, selection and opportunity-capture program; it must not rescue or continue ARP/Q-series hypotheses after their terminal stop rule.

targetOutputContract.probabilityRule: No field may be labelled probability/confidence-of-success unless it is empirically calibrated out-of-sample. Heuristic scores must be labelled score/rank only.

designRules: Market-family policies are permitted; post-outcome symbol/timeframe one-off patches are prohibited.
Instrument-contract rules are allowed only when they describe exogenous market mechanics and are declared before outcome inspection.
Entry quality must be separated from idea quality: a valid idea may return WAIT_FOR_ENTRY instead of forcing execution.
Stop placement is an invalidation/noise model, not a fixed percentage chosen to improve backtest hit rate.
Targets must be progressive and must combine market structure with volatility and realistic execution; synthetic R-multiple extension alone cannot create a target.
Costs, spread and slippage are part of the decision gate, not a reporting afterthought.
No automatic widening of a stop or extension of a target solely to make RR pass a threshold.
No auto-execution or broker order submission during research.

opportunityCaptureFramework.purpose: Measure both false positives and false negatives.
opportunityCaptureFramework.antiHindsightRule: Ex-post opportunity labels may be used only for audit/recall measurement. They may not become causal input features or be used to move a decision-time level.

stages: Phase 0 frozen baseline audit and metric lock
Phase 6 R15 integration candidate and full Senior Council release gate
multipleTestingControls: Probability of Backtest Overfitting/CSCV where sample geometry permits
validationProtocol.note: Promotion gates are deliberately portfolio-level plus breadth constraints; a market family may abstain when no robust edge is present. High trade frequency is not a target.

releaseRule: R16/ITE1 production integration is forbidden until the same frozen engine passes all required validation stages and then passes R15 parity, regression, static, mutation, package and live gates.

references.citation: Bailey, Borwein, Lopez de Prado & Zhu, The Probability of Backtest Overfitting, Journal of Computational Finance
Bailey & Lopez de Prado, The Deflated Sharpe Ratio, Journal of Portfolio Management 40(5)
Kaminski & Lo, When do stop-loss rules stop losses?, Journal of Financial Markets 18
